outcome: Etiological profile of early neonatal bacterial sepsis
Detection of pathogens causing early neonatal sepsis by multiplex qPCR
cohort: The study included 150 neonates diagnosed with clinical early neonatal sepsis and hospitalized in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), and 10 healthy control newborns.
finding: Multiplex qPCR revealed Escherichia coli (76%), Staphylococcus aureus (34%), and Streptococcus agalactiae (13.3%) as the predominant pathogens in neonates with clinical sepsis, demonstrating potential for rapid and sensitive detection compared to microbiological methods.
cross-section timing: Samples were collected from newborns at the time of their diagnosis with clinical early neonatal sepsis.
